nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$ and let $c$ assign a color in $K$ to every unordered pair of elements of $V$. If $c$ is a proper coloring of unordered pairs for $G$, then the edge labeling of $G$ that gives each edge $e$ the color $c(e)$ is a proper edge coloring of $G$.
nodes.title: Proper colorings of unordered pairs restrict to proper edge colorings

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$. An edge labeling $C$ of $G$ with colors in $K$ is a proper edge coloring when any two distinct edges of $G$ that share a vertex receive different colors: whenever a vertex $v$ is adjacent to $w_1$ and to $w_2$ with $w_1 \ne w_2$, the edges $v w_1$ and $v w_2$ have different colors under $C$.
nodes.title: Proper edge coloring

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$. A map $c$ that assigns a color in $K$ to every unordered pair of elements of $V$ is a proper coloring of unordered pairs for $G$ when, for all vertices $x, y, z$ such that $x$ is adjacent to both $y$ and $z$ and $y \ne z$, the pairs $\{x, y\}$ and $\{x, z\}$ receive different colors under $c$.
nodes.title: Proper coloring of unordered pairs

nodes.summary: König's line coloring, bounded-degree multigraph case: a bipartite multigraph of maximum degree at most `d` is `d`-edge-colorable. The proof pads both sides with dummy edges to reach the regular case. Shared API also used by the multigraph Galvin development.
nodes.title: König's edge coloring theorem for bounded-degree bipartite multigraphs

nodes.summary: König's line coloring, regular multigraph case: a `d`-regular bipartite multigraph (given by endpoint projections) is `d`-edge-colorable. The proof extracts a perfect matching by Hall's theorem and inducts. Shared API also used by the multigraph Galvin development.
nodes.title: König's edge coloring theorem for regular bipartite multigraphs

nodes.summary: Every finite bipartite simple graph $G$ has a proper edge coloring with $\Delta(G)$ colors, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$.
nodes.title: König's line coloring theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be simple graphs on $V$ such that every edge of $H$ is an edge of $G$. If a map $c$ from unordered pairs of elements of $V$ to $K$ is a proper coloring of unordered pairs for $G$, then it is also a proper coloring of unordered pairs for $H$.
nodes.title: Proper colorings of unordered pairs pass to subgraphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $\Delta$ be its maximum degree. Then $G$ has a proper edge coloring with $\Delta + 1$ colors: there is an assignment of colors from $\{0, 1, \dots, \Delta\}$ to the edges of $G$ such that any two distinct edges sharing a vertex receive different colors.
nodes.title: Vizing's theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
